title: Pichai Defends Google's AI Strategy as Investors Question Gemini Delays
excerpt: Alphabet's CEO pushed back against Wall Street concerns about falling behind in AI coding, pointing to 82% cloud growth and teasing the ambitious Gemini 4 model during the company's Q2 earnings call.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Google Cloud revenue soared 82% year-over-year, reaching $24.8 billion in Q2.
  • Sundar Pichai acknowledged the need for improvement in AI coding and agentic tasks.
  • Gemini 4 is teased as an ambitious model with monthly rollouts planned.
  • Alphabet raised its 2026 capital expenditure guidance by $15 billion to $195-$205 billion.
  • Shares fell roughly 4% in after-hours trading following the capex announcement.

Q2 earnings call

Alphabet CEO Sundar Pichai used the company's second-quarter earnings call on Wednesday to mount a forceful defense of Google's AI strategy, pushing back against growing investor anxiety that the search giant is losing ground to rivals in the fast-moving artificial intelligence race.

The earnings call came amid rising concern on Wall Street about Google's decision to delay the release of Gemini 3.5 Pro, a model originally scheduled for June that was expected to strengthen the company's position in AI coding and autonomous agent tasks — two of the industry's most fiercely contested areas.

Acknowledging the Gap

When pressed by JPMorgan analyst Doug Anmuth on whether Google's frontier models could remain competitive, Pichai struck an unusually candid tone.

https://x.com/moneycontrolcom/status/2080110719123783717

"We've had clearly frontier models. There are many attributes on which we are still at the frontier; there are areas where we've acknowledged we need to improve and coding and agentic coding is an example of that."

— Sundar Pichai, CEO, Alphabet

The admission is significant coming from the head of a company that has invested heavily in AI across its product lineup. Google's delayed Gemini 3.5 Pro release has fueled concerns that the company is losing momentum just as OpenAI, Anthropic, and a growing roster of Chinese competitors have accelerated their pace of model releases.

Rather than dwell on the delay, Pichai repeatedly highlighted Gemini Flash, Google's cheaper, faster "workhorse" model that powers applications spanning cybersecurity, customer-service agents, data analytics, and enterprise software. He pointed to the newly released Gemini 3.6 Flash, noting it improved by more than 10 points on a coding benchmark compared with the previous version while using fewer tokens. The company also unveiled Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and a cybersecurity-focused Flash Cyber model on Tuesday, according to Reuters.

Gemini 4 on the Horizon

Looking ahead, Pichai teased the upcoming Gemini 4, calling it a "very ambitious effort" trained on a substantially larger scale. When Barclays analyst Ross Sandler raised similar concerns about Google's model release pace, Pichai disclosed that the Gemini 4 roadmap includes rolling out models "almost at a monthly cadence."

https://youtube.com/watch?v=DN8R9YwcAR8

"I think people will be pleased" when Google unveils Gemini 4, Pichai said, adding that the company remains "very committed and very confident" about staying at the leading edge of AI.

Cloud Revenue Blows Past Estimates

Alphabet's financial results provided Pichai with strong ammunition. Google Cloud revenue surged 82% year-over-year to $24.8 billion in the June quarter, handily beating Wall Street's forecast of $22.5 billion and accelerating from 63% growth in Q1. The cloud business has benefited from growing deals for Google's custom TPU AI chips, including multibillion-dollar agreements with Meta Platforms and Anthropic.

Gemini Model Rollout Plans
›Gemini 4 is described as a 'very ambitious effort'.
›Models to be released 'almost at a monthly cadence'.
›Gemini 3.6 Flash improved coding benchmark by over 10 points.
›Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and Flash Cyber models announced.

Total revenue rose 24% to $119.8 billion, beating analyst expectations of $117.1 billion. Google's operating margin expanded two percentage points to 34%. Reported earnings per share hit $9.11, though a $98 billion surge in equity investments — largely tied to Alphabet's approximately 14% stake in Anthropic — inflated the headline number well above the $2.85 analysts expected on a normalized basis.

Google Services revenue increased 15% to $94.5 billion, with search advertising up 17% to $63.3 billion and YouTube ads rising 13% to $11.1 billion. Nearly 90% of the Fortune 100 are now using Gemini Enterprise, Pichai said.

Spending Surge Spooks Investors

Despite the strong top-line growth, investor attention snapped to Alphabet's capital expenditure plans. The company raised its 2026 capex guidance by $15 billion to a range of $195 billion to $205 billion, and signaled that 2027 spending could rise further. CFO Anat Ashkenazi added that Google plans to lease AI data center capacity from other cloud companies to meet customer demand, a move that could pressure profit margins.

Alphabet shares fell roughly 4% in after-hours trading. The stock has dropped about 9% since late April, weighed down by concerns over Gemini delays and several high-profile executive departures.

A Familiar Playbook for the Indian-Born CEO

Investor Concerns Rise

For Pichai, the challenge is a familiar one: persuading investors to judge Google's AI ambitions not by the delay of a single flagship model, but by the breadth of an ecosystem that spans cloud infrastructure, custom AI chips, and a portfolio of Gemini models embedded across its products. Google is the first of the Big Tech companies to report quarterly results this cycle, with Meta Platforms, Microsoft, and Amazon following next week.

The earnings call underscored a broader tension playing out across the AI industry — between the relentless pace of model releases that markets now demand and the methodical engineering approach that built Google's search dominance. Whether Gemini 4 can deliver on Pichai's promises will likely determine whether investors see Google as an AI leader or a well-funded follower.
